#!/bin/bash

# SECURITY: assign sanitized params to shell variables in an unquoted
# assignment slot, then reference them only as "$VAR". Never interpolate
#  inside a quoted context - sanitize() (shlex.quote) wraps
# dangerous values in single quotes, which are literal (and command
# substitution stays active) inside a double-quoted or single-quoted slot.
KIND=services
# 'namespace' is also a Jinja global (namespace()), so it is defined even when omitted
SEL_NAMESPACE=boutique
SEL_LABELS=
SEL_FIELDS=
# Strict tool calls send null for unset optional params, which renders as 'None'
[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" = "None" ] && SEL_NAMESPACE=""
[ "$SEL_LABELS" = "None" ] && SEL_LABELS=""
[ "$SEL_FIELDS" = "None" ] && SEL_FIELDS=""

# Collapse multi-line jq expressions (LLMs sometimes write multi-line jq)
# Note: use $'\n' syntax instead of '\n' because Jinja2 interprets \n as literal newlines
JQ_FILTER='.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, type: .spec.type, clusterIP: .spec.clusterIP, selector: .spec.selector, ports: .spec.ports}'
JQ_FILTER=$(printf '%s' "$JQ_FILTER" | tr $'\n\r' '  ')

err_file=$(mktemp)
PROCESSED=0
NOTES='[]'
SCOPE='null'

add_note() {
  NOTES=$(jq -c --arg note "$1" '. + [$note]' <<< "$NOTES")
}

uri_encode() {
  jq -rn --arg v "$1" '$v|@uri'
}

fail() {
  err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
  rm -f "$err_file"
  jq -n --arg stderr "$1 $err_content" --argjson total "$PROCESSED" --argjson notes "$NOTES" --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
    '{total_items_processed: $total, matches_found: 0, results: [], stderr: $stderr, scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
  exit 0
}

# The namespace becomes part of the raw API path, so anything other than a valid
# namespace name (e.g. 'default/services/x:80/proxy/?') could reach other API endpoints
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && ! [[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" =~ ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$ ]]; then
  fail "Invalid namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}': must be a Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase letters, digits and '-')."
fi

# Get the API path for the resource kind using kubectl
# Match the resource name (first column) as an EXACT string, not a
# grep regex - otherwise a kind like '.*' or 'a|b' would match the
# wrong resource.
CANDIDATES=$(kubectl api-resources --no-headers 2>>"$err_file" | awk -v kind="$KIND" '$1 == kind')
API_INFO=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | head -1)

# plural (e.g. Calico's crd.projectcalico.org networkpolicies) can be listed
# before networking.k8s.io. Pick what `kubectl get` picks: the core group,
# then the first group in server discovery order (/apis).
if [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -c .)" -gt 1 ] && [[ "$API_INFO" != *" v1 "* ]]; then
  API_GROUPS=$(kubectl get --raw /apis 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.groups[].name' 2>/dev/null)
  if [ -z "$API_GROUPS" ]; then
    add_note "Several API groups serve '${KIND}' and server discovery (/apis) failed, so the first group listed by kubectl api-resources was used."
  fi
  for group in $API_GROUPS; do
    match=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -F " $group/" | head -1)
    if [ -n "$match" ]; then
      API_INFO="$match"
      break
    fi
  done
fi

if [ -z "$API_INFO" ]; then
  fail "Unable to find resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Extract NAMESPACED value
if [[ "$API_INFO" == *" true "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=true
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ true .*//')
elif [[ "$API_INFO" == *" false "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=false
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ false .*//')
else
  fail "Could not parse API info for '${KIND}'."
fi

# Trim trailing spaces from prefix and collapse internal spaces
PREFIX=$(echo "$PREFIX" | sed 's/  *$//' | sed 's/  */ /g')

IFS=' ' read -ra PREFIX_FIELDS <<< "$PREFIX"
FIELD_COUNT=0
for field in "${PREFIX_FIELDS[@]}"; do
  ((FIELD_COUNT++))
done

RESOURCE_NAME="${PREFIX_FIELDS[0]}"
if [ $FIELD_COUNT -ge 2 ]; then

fi

# cluster-scoped kinds ignore the namespace (as kubectl does)

  API_BASE="/apis/${API_VERSION}"
fi

  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/namespaces/${SEL_NAMESPACE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"

  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&labelSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_LABELS")"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_FIELDS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&fieldSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_FIELDS")"
fi

SCOPE=$(jq -nc --arg resource "$RESOURCE_NAME" --arg api_version "$API_VERSION" \
  --arg namespace "$SEL_NAMESPACE" --arg labels "$SEL_LABELS" --arg fields "$SEL_FIELDS" \
  '{resource: $resource, api_version: $api_version,
    namespace: (if $namespace == "" then null else $namespace end),
    label_selector: (if $labels == "" then null else $labels end),
    field_selector: (if $fields == "" then null else $fields end)}')

CONTINUE=""
TOTAL_MATCHES=0

  QUERY="${API_PATH}?limit=${LIMIT}${SELECTOR_QUERY}"
  if [ -n "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    # continue tokens are base64 and may contain '+', '/' or '='
    QUERY="${QUERY}&continue=$(uri_encode "$CONTINUE")"
  fi

  OUTPUT=$(kubectl get --raw "$QUERY" 2>>"$err_file")
  exit_code=$?

  if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "kubectl get --raw failed for $QUERY."
  fi

  ITEMS_COUNT=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq '.items | length')

  MATCHES=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -c "$JQ_FILTER" 2>>"$err_file")
  jq_exit=$?
  if [ $jq_exit -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "jq expression failed."
  fi

  if [ "$ITEMS_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
    if [ -n "$MATCHES" ]; then

        ALL_MATCHES="$MATCHES"
      else
        ALL_MATCHES="$ALL_MATCHES"$'\n'"$MATCHES"
      fi
      MATCH_COUNT=$(echo "$MATCHES" | grep -c . || true)
      TOTAL_MATCHES=$((TOTAL_MATCHES + MATCH_COUNT))
    fi
    PROCESSED=$((PROCESSED + ITEMS_COUNT))
  fi

  CONTINUE=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -r '.metadata.continue // empty')

  if [ -z "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    break
  fi

err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
rm -f "$err_file"

# Output results as a JSON object with metadata. Results go through stdin, not --argjson:
# Linux caps a single argument at 128KB, so larger results failed with "Argument list too long".
printf '%s\n' "$ALL_MATCHES" | jq -s \
  --argjson total_items_processed "$PROCESSED" \
  --argjson matches_found "$TOTAL_MATCHES" \
  --arg stderr "$err_content" \
  --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
  --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
  '{total_items_processed: $total_items_processed, matches_found: $matches_found, results: ., stderr: (if $stderr == "" then null else $stderr end), scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'

#!/bin/bash

# assignment slot, then reference them only as "$VAR". Never interpolate
#  inside a quoted context - sanitize() (shlex.quote) wraps
# dangerous values in single quotes, which are literal (and command
# substitution stays active) inside a double-quoted or single-quoted slot.

# 'namespace' is also a Jinja global (namespace()), so it is defined even when omitted
SEL_NAMESPACE=boutique
SEL_LABELS=
SEL_FIELDS=
# Strict tool calls send null for unset optional params, which renders as 'None'
[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" = "None" ] && SEL_NAMESPACE=""
[ "$SEL_LABELS" = "None" ] && SEL_LABELS=""
[ "$SEL_FIELDS" = "None" ] && SEL_FIELDS=""

# Collapse multi-line jq expressions (LLMs sometimes write multi-line jq)
# Note: use $'\n' syntax instead of '\n' because Jinja2 interprets \n as literal newlines

JQ_FILTER=$(printf '%s' "$JQ_FILTER" | tr $'\n\r' '  ')

err_file=$(mktemp)
PROCESSED=0
NOTES='[]'
SCOPE='null'

add_note() {
  NOTES=$(jq -c --arg note "$1" '. + [$note]' <<< "$NOTES")
}

uri_encode() {
  jq -rn --arg v "$1" '$v|@uri'
}

  err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
  rm -f "$err_file"
  jq -n --arg stderr "$1 $err_content" --argjson total "$PROCESSED" --argjson notes "$NOTES" --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
    '{total_items_processed: $total, matches_found: 0, results: [], stderr: $stderr, scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
  exit 0
}

# The namespace becomes part of the raw API path, so anything other than a valid
# namespace name (e.g. 'default/services/x:80/proxy/?') could reach other API endpoints
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && ! [[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" =~ ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$ ]]; then
  fail "Invalid namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}': must be a Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase letters, digits and '-')."
fi

# Match the resource name (first column) as an EXACT string, not a
# grep regex - otherwise a kind like '.*' or 'a|b' would match the
# wrong resource.

# plural (e.g. Calico's crd.projectcalico.org networkpolicies) can be listed

# then the first group in server discovery order (/apis).

    match=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -F " $group/" | head -1)

      break
    fi

fi

  NAMESPACED=true
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ true .*//')
elif [[ "$API_INFO" == *" false "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=false

fi

# cluster-scoped kinds ignore the namespace (as kubectl does)

  fi

if [ -n "$SEL_LABELS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&labelSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_LABELS")"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_FIELDS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&fieldSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_FIELDS")"
fi

SCOPE=$(jq -nc --arg resource "$RESOURCE_NAME" --arg api_version "$API_VERSION" \
  --arg namespace "$SEL_NAMESPACE" --arg labels "$SEL_LABELS" --arg fields "$SEL_FIELDS" \
  '{resource: $resource, api_version: $api_version,

    label_selector: (if $labels == "" then null else $labels end),
    field_selector: (if $fields == "" then null else $fields end)}')

CONTINUE=""
TOTAL_MATCHES=0
ALL_MATCHES=""

while true; do

  if [ -n "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    # continue tokens are base64 and may contain '+', '/' or '='

  fi

  exit_code=$?

  if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "kubectl get --raw failed for $QUERY."
  fi

      TOTAL_MATCHES=$((TOTAL_MATCHES + MATCH_COUNT))
    fi
    PROCESSED=$((PROCESSED + ITEMS_COUNT))
  fi

  CONTINUE=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -r '.metadata.continue // empty')

  if [ -z "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    break
  fi
done

err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
rm -f "$err_file"

# Output results as a JSON object with metadata. Results go through stdin, not --argjson:
# Linux caps a single argument at 128KB, so larger results failed with "Argument list too long".
printf '%s\n' "$ALL_MATCHES" | jq -s \
  --argjson total_items_processed "$PROCESSED" \
  --argjson matches_found "$TOTAL_MATCHES" \
  --arg stderr "$err_content" \
  --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
  --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
  '{total_items_processed: $total_items_processed, matches_found: $matches_found, results: ., stderr: (if $stderr == "" then null else $stderr end), scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'

#!/bin/bash

# SECURITY: assign sanitized params to shell variables in an unquoted
# assignment slot, then reference them only as "$VAR". Never interpolate
#  inside a quoted context - sanitize() (shlex.quote) wraps
# dangerous values in single quotes, which are literal (and command
# substitution stays active) inside a double-quoted or single-quoted slot.
KIND=events
# 'namespace' is also a Jinja global (namespace()), so it is defined even when omitted
SEL_NAMESPACE=boutique
SEL_LABELS=
SEL_FIELDS=
# Strict tool calls send null for unset optional params, which renders as 'None'
[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" = "None" ] && SEL_NAMESPACE=""
[ "$SEL_LABELS" = "None" ] && SEL_LABELS=""
[ "$SEL_FIELDS" = "None" ] && SEL_FIELDS=""

# Collapse multi-line jq expressions (LLMs sometimes write multi-line jq)
# Note: use $'\n' syntax instead of '\n' because Jinja2 interprets \n as literal newlines
JQ_FILTER='.items[] | select(.lastTimestamp > "2026-11-17T08:20:00Z" or .eventTime > "2026-11-17T08:20:00Z") | {type, reason, obj: (.involvedObject.kind + "/" + .involvedObject.name), msg: .message, t: (.lastTimestamp // .eventTime)}'
JQ_FILTER=$(printf '%s' "$JQ_FILTER" | tr $'\n\r' '  ')

err_file=$(mktemp)
PROCESSED=0
NOTES='[]'
SCOPE='null'

add_note() {
  NOTES=$(jq -c --arg note "$1" '. + [$note]' <<< "$NOTES")
}

uri_encode() {
  jq -rn --arg v "$1" '$v|@uri'
}

fail() {
  err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
  rm -f "$err_file"
  jq -n --arg stderr "$1 $err_content" --argjson total "$PROCESSED" --argjson notes "$NOTES" --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
    '{total_items_processed: $total, matches_found: 0, results: [], stderr: $stderr, scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
  exit 0
}

# The namespace becomes part of the raw API path, so anything other than a valid
# namespace name (e.g. 'default/services/x:80/proxy/?') could reach other API endpoints
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && ! [[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" =~ ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$ ]]; then
  fail "Invalid namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}': must be a Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase letters, digits and '-')."
fi

# Match the resource name (first column) as an EXACT string, not a
# grep regex - otherwise a kind like '.*' or 'a|b' would match the
# wrong resource.
CANDIDATES=$(kubectl api-resources --no-headers 2>>"$err_file" | awk -v kind="$KIND" '$1 == kind')
API_INFO=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | head -1)

# plural (e.g. Calico's crd.projectcalico.org networkpolicies) can be listed
# before networking.k8s.io. Pick what `kubectl get` picks: the core group,
# then the first group in server discovery order (/apis).

  if [ -z "$API_GROUPS" ]; then
    add_note "Several API groups serve '${KIND}' and server discovery (/apis) failed, so the first group listed by kubectl api-resources was used."
  fi
  for group in $API_GROUPS; do
    match=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -F " $group/" | head -1)
    if [ -n "$match" ]; then
      API_INFO="$match"
      break
    fi
  done
fi

if [ -z "$API_INFO" ]; then
  fail "Unable to find resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Extract NAMESPACED value
if [[ "$API_INFO" == *" true "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=true
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ true .*//')
elif [[ "$API_INFO" == *" false "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=false
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ false .*//')
else
  fail "Could not parse API info for '${KIND}'."
fi

# Trim trailing spaces from prefix and collapse internal spaces
PREFIX=$(echo "$PREFIX" | sed 's/  *$//' | sed 's/  */ /g')

IFS=' ' read -ra PREFIX_FIELDS <<< "$PREFIX"
FIELD_COUNT=0
for field in "${PREFIX_FIELDS[@]}"; do
  ((FIELD_COUNT++))
done

RESOURCE_NAME="${PREFIX_FIELDS[0]}"
if [ $FIELD_COUNT -ge 2 ]; then
  API_VERSION="${PREFIX_FIELDS[$((FIELD_COUNT - 1))]}"
else
  API_VERSION=""
fi

if [ -z "$API_VERSION" ] || [ -z "$RESOURCE_NAME" ]; then
  fail "Unable to parse API info for resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Build API path: namespaced kinds can be listed within one namespace;
# cluster-scoped kinds ignore the namespace (as kubectl does)
if [[ "$API_VERSION" == "v1" ]]; then
  API_BASE="/api/v1"
else
  API_BASE="/apis/${API_VERSION}"
fi

  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/namespaces/${SEL_NAMESPACE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"

    add_note "namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}' ignored: ${RESOURCE_NAME} is cluster-scoped."
    SEL_NAMESPACE=""
  fi
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
fi

SELECTOR_QUERY=""
if [ -n "$SEL_LABELS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&labelSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_LABELS")"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_FIELDS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&fieldSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_FIELDS")"
fi

SCOPE=$(jq -nc --arg resource "$RESOURCE_NAME" --arg api_version "$API_VERSION" \
  --arg namespace "$SEL_NAMESPACE" --arg labels "$SEL_LABELS" --arg fields "$SEL_FIELDS" \
  '{resource: $resource, api_version: $api_version,
    namespace: (if $namespace == "" then null else $namespace end),
    label_selector: (if $labels == "" then null else $labels end),
    field_selector: (if $fields == "" then null else $fields end)}')

# Process resources in chunks using API pagination
LIMIT=500
CONTINUE=""
TOTAL_MATCHES=0
ALL_MATCHES=""

while true; do
  QUERY="${API_PATH}?limit=${LIMIT}${SELECTOR_QUERY}"
  if [ -n "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    # continue tokens are base64 and may contain '+', '/' or '='
    QUERY="${QUERY}&continue=$(uri_encode "$CONTINUE")"
  fi

  OUTPUT=$(kubectl get --raw "$QUERY" 2>>"$err_file")
  exit_code=$?

  if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "kubectl get --raw failed for $QUERY."
  fi

  ITEMS_COUNT=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq '.items | length')

  MATCHES=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -c "$JQ_FILTER" 2>>"$err_file")
  jq_exit=$?
  if [ $jq_exit -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "jq expression failed."
  fi

  if [ "$ITEMS_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
    if [ -n "$MATCHES" ]; then
      if [ -z "$ALL_MATCHES" ]; then
        ALL_MATCHES="$MATCHES"
      else
        ALL_MATCHES="$ALL_MATCHES"$'\n'"$MATCHES"
      fi
      MATCH_COUNT=$(echo "$MATCHES" | grep -c . || true)
      TOTAL_MATCHES=$((TOTAL_MATCHES + MATCH_COUNT))
    fi
    PROCESSED=$((PROCESSED + ITEMS_COUNT))
  fi

  CONTINUE=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -r '.metadata.continue // empty')

  if [ -z "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    break
  fi
done

err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
rm -f "$err_file"

# Output results as a JSON object with metadata. Results go through stdin, not --argjson:
# Linux caps a single argument at 128KB, so larger results failed with "Argument list too long".
printf '%s\n' "$ALL_MATCHES" | jq -s \
  --argjson total_items_processed "$PROCESSED" \
  --argjson matches_found "$TOTAL_MATCHES" \
  --arg stderr "$err_content" \
  --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
  --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
  '{total_items_processed: $total_items_processed, matches_found: $matches_found, results: ., stderr: (if $stderr == "" then null else $stderr end), scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'

    namespace: (if $namespace == "" then null else $namespace end),
    label_selector: (if $labels == "" then null else $labels end),
    field_selector: (if $fields == "" then null else $fields end)}')

# Process resources in chunks using API pagination
LIMIT=500
CONTINUE=""
TOTAL_MATCHES=0
ALL_MATCHES=""

while true; do
  QUERY="${API_PATH}?limit=${LIMIT}${SELECTOR_QUERY}"
  if [ -n "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    # continue tokens are base64 and may contain '+', '/' or '='
    QUERY="${QUERY}&continue=$(uri_encode "$CONTINUE")"

  exit_code=$?

  if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then

  MATCHES=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -c "$JQ_FILTER" 2>>"$err_file")
  jq_exit=$?
  if [ $jq_exit -ne 0 ]; then

      if [ -z "$ALL_MATCHES" ]; then

  --argjson total_items_processed "$PROCESSED" \

#!/bin/bash

# SECURITY: assign sanitized params to shell variables in an unquoted
# assignment slot, then reference them only as "$VAR". Never interpolate
#  inside a quoted context - sanitize() (shlex.quote) wraps
# dangerous values in single quotes, which are literal (and command
# substitution stays active) inside a double-quoted or single-quoted slot.
KIND=configmaps
# 'namespace' is also a Jinja global (namespace()), so it is defined even when omitted
SEL_NAMESPACE=boutique
SEL_LABELS=
SEL_FIELDS=
# Strict tool calls send null for unset optional params, which renders as 'None'
[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" = "None" ] && SEL_NAMESPACE=""
[ "$SEL_LABELS" = "None" ] && SEL_LABELS=""
[ "$SEL_FIELDS" = "None" ] && SEL_FIELDS=""

# Collapse multi-line jq expressions (LLMs sometimes write multi-line jq)
# Note: use $'\n' syntax instead of '\n' because Jinja2 interprets \n as literal newlines
JQ_FILTER='.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, data: (.data | keys)}'
JQ_FILTER=$(printf '%s' "$JQ_FILTER" | tr $'\n\r' '  ')

err_file=$(mktemp)
PROCESSED=0
NOTES='[]'
SCOPE='null'

add_note() {
  NOTES=$(jq -c --arg note "$1" '. + [$note]' <<< "$NOTES")
}

uri_encode() {
  jq -rn --arg v "$1" '$v|@uri'
}

fail() {
  err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
  rm -f "$err_file"
  jq -n --arg stderr "$1 $err_content" --argjson total "$PROCESSED" --argjson notes "$NOTES" --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
    '{total_items_processed: $total, matches_found: 0, results: [], stderr: $stderr, scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
  exit 0
}

# The namespace becomes part of the raw API path, so anything other than a valid
# namespace name (e.g. 'default/services/x:80/proxy/?') could reach other API endpoints
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && ! [[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" =~ ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$ ]]; then
  fail "Invalid namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}': must be a Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase letters, digits and '-')."
fi

# Get the API path for the resource kind using kubectl
# Match the resource name (first column) as an EXACT string, not a
# grep regex - otherwise a kind like '.*' or 'a|b' would match the
# wrong resource.
CANDIDATES=$(kubectl api-resources --no-headers 2>>"$err_file" | awk -v kind="$KIND" '$1 == kind')
API_INFO=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | head -1)
# `kubectl api-resources` sorts by group name, so a CRD reusing a built-in
# plural (e.g. Calico's crd.projectcalico.org networkpolicies) can be listed
# before networking.k8s.io. Pick what `kubectl get` picks: the core group,
# then the first group in server discovery order (/apis).
if [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -c .)" -gt 1 ] && [[ "$API_INFO" != *" v1 "* ]]; then
  API_GROUPS=$(kubectl get --raw /apis 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.groups[].name' 2>/dev/null)
  if [ -z "$API_GROUPS" ]; then
    add_note "Several API groups serve '${KIND}' and server discovery (/apis) failed, so the first group listed by kubectl api-resources was used."
  fi
  for group in $API_GROUPS; do
    match=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -F " $group/" | head -1)
    if [ -n "$match" ]; then
      API_INFO="$match"
      break
    fi
  done
fi

if [ -z "$API_INFO" ]; then
  fail "Unable to find resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Extract NAMESPACED value
if [[ "$API_INFO" == *" true "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=true
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ true .*//')
elif [[ "$API_INFO" == *" false "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=false
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ false .*//')
else
  fail "Could not parse API info for '${KIND}'."
fi

# Trim trailing spaces from prefix and collapse internal spaces
PREFIX=$(echo "$PREFIX" | sed 's/  *$//' | sed 's/  */ /g')

IFS=' ' read -ra PREFIX_FIELDS <<< "$PREFIX"
FIELD_COUNT=0
for field in "${PREFIX_FIELDS[@]}"; do
  ((FIELD_COUNT++))
done

RESOURCE_NAME="${PREFIX_FIELDS[0]}"
if [ $FIELD_COUNT -ge 2 ]; then
  API_VERSION="${PREFIX_FIELDS[$((FIELD_COUNT - 1))]}"
else
  API_VERSION=""
fi

if [ -z "$API_VERSION" ] || [ -z "$RESOURCE_NAME" ]; then
  fail "Unable to parse API info for resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Build API path: namespaced kinds can be listed within one namespace;
# cluster-scoped kinds ignore the namespace (as kubectl does)
if [[ "$API_VERSION" == "v1" ]]; then
  API_BASE="/api/v1"
else
  API_BASE="/apis/${API_VERSION}"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && [ "$NAMESPACED" = "true" ]; then
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/namespaces/${SEL_NAMESPACE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
else
  if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ]; then
    add_note "namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}' ignored: ${RESOURCE_NAME} is cluster-scoped."
    SEL_NAMESPACE=""
  fi
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
fi

SELECTOR_QUERY=""
if [ -n "$SEL_LABELS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&labelSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_LABELS")"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_FIELDS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&fieldSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_FIELDS")"
fi

SCOPE=$(jq -nc --arg resource "$RESOURCE_NAME" --arg api_version "$API_VERSION" \
  --arg namespace "$SEL_NAMESPACE" --arg labels "$SEL_LABELS" --arg fields "$SEL_FIELDS" \
  '{resource: $resource, api_version: $api_version,
    namespace: (if $namespace == "" then null else $namespace end),
    label_selector: (if $labels == "" then null else $labels end),
    field_selector: (if $fields == "" then null else $fields end)}')

# Process resources in chunks using API pagination
LIMIT=500
CONTINUE=""
TOTAL_MATCHES=0
ALL_MATCHES=""

while true; do
  QUERY="${API_PATH}?limit=${LIMIT}${SELECTOR_QUERY}"
  if [ -n "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    # continue tokens are base64 and may contain '+', '/' or '='
    QUERY="${QUERY}&continue=$(uri_encode "$CONTINUE")"
  fi

  OUTPUT=$(kubectl get --raw "$QUERY" 2>>"$err_file")
  exit_code=$?

  if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "kubectl get --raw failed for $QUERY."
  fi

  ITEMS_COUNT=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq '.items | length')

  MATCHES=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -c "$JQ_FILTER" 2>>"$err_file")
  jq_exit=$?
  if [ $jq_exit -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "jq expression failed."
  fi

  if [ "$ITEMS_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
    if [ -n "$MATCHES" ]; then
      if [ -z "$ALL_MATCHES" ]; then
        ALL_MATCHES="$MATCHES"
      else
        ALL_MATCHES="$ALL_MATCHES"$'\n'"$MATCHES"
      fi
      MATCH_COUNT=$(echo "$MATCHES" | grep -c . || true)
      TOTAL_MATCHES=$((TOTAL_MATCHES + MATCH_COUNT))
    fi
    PROCESSED=$((PROCESSED + ITEMS_COUNT))
  fi

  CONTINUE=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -r '.metadata.continue // empty')

  if [ -z "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    break
  fi
done

err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
rm -f "$err_file"

# Output results as a JSON object with metadata. Results go through stdin, not --argjson:
# Linux caps a single argument at 128KB, so larger results failed with "Argument list too long".
printf '%s\n' "$ALL_MATCHES" | jq -s \
  --argjson total_items_processed "$PROCESSED" \
  --argjson matches_found "$TOTAL_MATCHES" \
  --arg stderr "$err_content" \
  --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
  --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
  '{total_items_processed: $total_items_processed, matches_found: $matches_found, results: ., stderr: (if $stderr == "" then null else $stderr end), scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'

## 第 3 轮实测结果（对照前两轮预期）

**被推翻的判断**

- 第 2 轮「首页快 ⇒ 问题锁定在 recommendationservice 这一跳」——**推翻**。同一时间窗（08:30:05–08:31:00）我把首页也取了：13 个首页请求里 `216ms`、`157ms`、`67ms`、`44ms`、`39ms` 都有（`edd40ceb` start 08:30:07.162 → end 07.378 = 216ms）。首页同样被卡。前一轮"0/9"是小样本。
- 第 1 轮「各服务自身 CPU 节流」——**推翻**（上一轮已证），且本轮新证据表明与单个 Pod 的 quota 无关（见下）。
- 第 2 轮「~200ms ≈ TCP RTO_MIN 的单包重传」——**基本排除**（见下，恢复时刻是全局同步的，不是每流独立的）。

**本轮新增的关键证据：停顿是"整机同时冻结，然后同时恢复"**

用 frontend 的 `request started/complete` + 各后端日志的到达时间做逐请求对齐（08:30 窗口），发现多个**互不相关的请求在同一微秒级时刻一起结束**：

| 时刻 | 现象 |
|---|---|
| 08:30:34.6243 / .6247 | `33f91b3d`（start 34.513，111ms，product 页）与 `f9663eb0`（start 34.615，9ms）**同时完成** |
| 08:30:46.7297 | `1ae4e810`（start 46.669，60ms）与 `2cd3489a`（start 46.718，11ms）**同时完成** |
| 08:30:51.3366 | `090c865e`（start 51.201，135ms）与 `ed97221c`（start 51.327，9ms）**同时完成** |
| 08:30:46.728 / 51.335 | adservice **两个线程**（executor-7、executor-2）在同一毫秒收到请求 |
| 08:30:46.7255/.7262、51.3326/.3329 | recommendationservice 成对（<1ms）收到**不同**前端请求 |

不同服务、不同连接、不同请求在**同一瞬间恢复推进** —— 这只能是节点/整机层面在这些窗口里"没有调度任何东西"，不符合单条 TCP 流丢包重传（那样各流恢复时刻是错开的），也不符合某个 Pod 自身 CFS quota（只影响该 Pod）。

停顿长度分布也支持这点：`50/60/67/96/111/126/135/149/157/183ms` 的连续谱 + 主峰 `209–237ms` + 叠加值 `425/436ms` 和一次 `862ms`；按 196 请求/75s、21.9% 命中率反推，约 **1 次/秒** 的 ~200ms 整机冻结。

**同样被证实/加固的事实**

- 12 个 Pod（含 loadgenerator）全部在 `tiktok-k8s-lab-control-plane` 一个节点上；CPU requests 合计约 **1.57 核**（loadgenerator 300m 是最大单一消费者）。
- 稳态 kubelet 探针也撞上同一停顿：`productcatalogservice-7457c7c77f-6l4dm`（08:17 起运行）在 **08:29:20 Liveness "failed to connect 10.244.0.206:3550 within 1s"**。

- 逐跳分解（product 页）：停顿落在 `GetProduct`、`currencies→rec` 段、以及 `rec 收到后` 段——**分散在所有跳**，不存在单一"慢服务"。cart 页（不调用 adservice）同样 219–231ms，adservice 也排除（adservice 收包数 89 ≈ 同窗口 product 76 + home 13，说明 ads 只被 home/product 调用）。

# Investigation guidelines

* Gather data with as many tool calls as needed before responding; keep going until you reach the deepest root cause you can find.
* Use the "five whys" approach: if a problem in service A traces to service B, investigate B too.

* Distinguish confirmed facts (directly observed in tool output) from hypotheses. Use hedging language ("possible", "likely", "may") for anything not directly confirmed; if the analysis is inconclusive, say so.
* Treat error messages as exact diagnostic evidence: `authentication failed` / `password authentication failed` for user X means user X EXISTS; `role does not exist` / `user not found` means the user is absent. These are mutually exclusive — never add "or the user may not exist" to an authentication failure.
* Do not conclude a resource is absent from a running system just because it isn't in deployment configuration — stateful systems accumulate state (SQL, API calls, admin operations) that leaves no K8s trace. If you can't read a value (e.g. a Secret), say you couldn't verify it rather than guessing.
* Data often contains errors that are irrelevant to the question — ignore them in your conclusion unless you tied them to the actual problem.
* ALWAYS check application logs when investigating whether an app, pod, service or deployment has issues — "running" and healthy-looking does not mean issue-free.

# Impact and blast radius

* Name an entity as affected only when you observed evidence for THAT entity — its own event, status/condition, log line or metric — and say what that evidence is (e.g. "`checkout-cache`: Evicted event, now Pending").
* Never widen the blast radius by inference. A node condition does not tell you which pods it hit; a failing dependency does not tell you which of its clients broke; an unhealthy shared component does not mean its consumers are unhealthy. Check each entity before you name it, or do not name it — sampling a workload's replicas characterizes the WORKLOAD, so attribute what you found to it rather than to replicas you did not look at.
* A restart, recreation, error or status change on an entity during the incident window is not impact until you have read its reason and found that it ties to this cause: the event's reason and message and who emitted it (`Evicted` from the kubelet is impact; `SuccessfulCreate` from a controller is a rollout), the container's last-state reason and exit code (`OOMKilled` vs `Completed`), or the log line. A pod that is 5 minutes old on a node that had trouble 5 minutes ago was not necessarily evicted — check what created it. Coincidence in time is not causation, and "also affected" is a claim that needs its own evidence.
* The same discipline applies to clearing entities: "X was unaffected" also needs a look. If you did not check, say you did not check.
* Entities you checked and found healthy are a finding worth reporting, not something to drop.
* Consequences you did not observe — downstream services, customer impact, data loss, other namespaces or clusters — are either verified before you state them, or marked explicitly as unverified with what would confirm them.
* Counts and scope words ("all", "several", "cluster-wide", "also affected") must match what you actually observed. Do not generalize from a sample you did not take.
* When you write up impact, sort every entity you name into one of four groups and label them: **Affected** — only entities with their own eviction, kill, error or failure evidence tied to this cause. Every line here quotes the exact reason token that proves it, in parentheses: `Evicted`, `OOMKilled`, `BackOff`, `Failed`, `Unhealthy` on a long-running pod, an error log line. If you cannot quote such a token for that entity, it does not go here — `SuccessfulDelete`, `SuccessfulCreate`, `Scheduled`, `Started` and a probe miss at startup are not among them. A recreation, restart or probe miss inside the window is never enough on its own, whatever sub-label you give it; **Checked, healthy** — you looked and found nothing wrong; **Changed during the window for another reason** — it restarted, was recreated or errored, and you name what did it (a controller rollout, a scheduled job, an operator, a probe at startup) and how you know; **Not checked**. Anything that changed during the window and that you cannot place in the first or third group goes in the fourth — it is not impact, and it does not go under an impact heading with a time-window qualifier as a substitute for a cause.

messages.reasoning_content:
The events confirm pod churn from our own rollouts/reverts. Note readiness probe failures happen on new pods (startup), which is normal-ish. But productcatalogservice liveness probe failed at 08:29:20 on a pod started 08:17:09 — that's a steady-state failure! Interesting. That pod has been running since 08:17 and its liveness probe at 08:29:20 failed with "failed to connect service 10.244.0.206:3550 within 1s". So productcatalogservice occasionally fails to accept a TCP connection within 1s. That's a real signal: >1s stall in connect.

Hmm, but the readiness/liveness probes come from kubelet on the same node going to the pod IP. If connect takes >1s occasionally, that's a strong indicator of a network/node-level stall, affecting even loopback-ish pod-to-pod.

Let me get deployment specs properly (env with null-safe).

Now, let me look at the frontend logs to characterize current latency and see which operations are slow. Actually more valuable: examine whether there's a specific service with an app-level periodic stall.

Hmm, wait. Important thought: the ~200ms slow factor of ~20%. What if one of the services is being hit by a periodic CPU-heavy thing... but CPU limits raised didn't help.

New angle: what about DNS? A "5s" DNS timeout would be visible. No.

What about the "cartservice" .NET GC? POST /cart sometimes 206ms. cartservice is .NET; redis-cart.

Let me reconsider: is there any evidence that the delay is a *single* service's occasional stall vs network? The instruction: distinguish. The probes failing to connect within 1s to productcatalogservice pod IPs at steady state (pod running 12 min, liveness fails) is quite telling: at 08:29:20 the pod's kubelet probe couldn't establish TCP to 10.244.0.206:3550 within 1s. If the app were CPU-starved, that's possible too (productcatalog with 200m limit... but cpu limits were raised to 500m during round 1 and reverted at 08:25; now 200m again).

Hold on — round 1 raised productcatalog to 500m, and 08:17:09 pod restarted after revert? Actually the current pod 6l4dm started 08:17:09 — that's during round 1 (limits raised). Revert at 08:25 would have restarted pods... Wait cartservice, frontend, productcatalog, redis-cart, recommendationservice pods started at 08:17:09 — hmm, and events show currencyservice/recommendationservice churn at 08:25-08:28. cartservice's pod started 08:17:09 (round 1's rollout from 08:06-ish? no, round 1 was at ~08:17).

Anyway, current limits: most 200m.

Now what is actually stalling? Let me gather app logs. Frontend logs show request durations. Let me get frontend logs for last ~5 minutes with no filter and large limit to compute distribution myself. That's the key measurement. Then, correlate with downstream service logs.

Actually a cleverer approach: use frontend logs to identify the slow request's product IDs and then check productcatalog/recommendationservice logs at those timestamps.

Given limited rounds, let me consider what pod-level action could plausibly work. Round 3 is last. If the root cause is node/CNI, no pod-level action helps; I should report with empty actions? But "最后一个 json 里 actions 可以为空数组" if no action fixes it.

But wait. Think again about candidate root causes not yet explored:

(a) The frontend pod and all others on same node — the loadgenerator is also there with 500m limit and 300m request. The loadgenerator drives traffic. If loadgenerator itself gets throttled... it would slow request *rate*, not latency.

(b) What about `frontend` — it has a "currency conversion" step, and there's `setCurrency`. Round 1 found setCurrency 0ms.

(c) A key thought: ~20% of requests slow by ~200ms, all hops affected randomly. On a single-node cluster with CFS quota, per-pod CPU throttling gives exactly this: a pod hitting its quota stalls until the next 100ms period. But raising limits to 1 CPU didn't help. Unless... the limits were raised but *requests* stayed low, and the node is oversubscribed, so throttling came from node-level CPU contention instead of CFS quota. Hmm, though raising CPU limits would reduce CFS throttle accounting (throttle is per-cgroup quota).

(d) Could there be an "etc/hosts" or a slow `/etc/resolv.conf` due to DNS? DNS lookups on each request: Go gRPC client resolves on new connection. If it reconnects... With 200ms RTO... hmm.

(e) What about a Service whose targetPort points to something wrong? All services look correct: emailservice 5000→8080 (correct), frontend 80→8080 correct.

(f) Hmm, what about a **NetworkPolicy** or **conntrack**? Let me check networkpolicies.

(g) What about a node-level pod outside boutique, e.g. a chaos daemon? I can't list nodes but maybe I can list pods in other namespaces? Let me try listing pods cluster-wide (namespace null). If allowed, I could see other workloads on the same node (e.g., a CPU hog, or something like `stress` pod).

That's a high-value check: cluster-wide pods listing. Also check for CRDs of chaos (may be forbidden).

Let me also check resourcequota/limitrange in boutique (a LimitRange could impose CPU limits... e.g., default limit 200m! Interesting: most deployments show limit 200m and request 100m — that looks like defaults possibly from a LimitRange). But that wouldn't cause 200ms stalls.

Let me look for other namespaces with pods on the same node.

Let me check: home requests at 08:29:18.274 (16ms), 22.849 (39), 23.941 (14), 24.517 (12), 29.311 (40), 31.317 (22), 32.627 (15). All fast! That's 7 home requests, zero slow. So it really is the recommendations hop: ~50% of /product requests and ~60% of /cart requests now slow?! Earlier 25%. Hmm interesting, seems worse now.

Wait! Important: maybe rec's call goes to a *stale* endpoint. Round 2 set PRODUCT_CATALOG_SERVICE_ADDR to the ClusterIP 10.96.32.253. That was reverted? "每一轮的改动已全部撤销（重建过的 Pod 除外）". Let me fetch rec logs and productcatalog logs.

Actually, here's another very plausible root cause I should test: productcatalogservice pod 6l4dm has liveness probe failing at 08:29:20 in steady state — "failed to connect within 1s". That means at 08:29:20 the productcatalog pod didn't accept a TCP connection within 1s. But home page requests (which call productcatalog) at 08:29:23.9 etc. were fast. And rec's channel to productcatalog is also long-lived. So the probe timeout is a separate thing — but it indicates the pod occasionally can't accept new TCP connections for >1s. That's an app-level accept stall, suggestive of the same underlying stall (200ms-1s+) happening in productcatalog.

Hmm! This makes productcatalog interesting again: it fails to accept new connections >1s. Why? Go service, ListenAndServe, accept is fast. Unless the process is CPU-starved (200m limit) or blocked. But it's got 100m request/200m limit on a node with many pods.

Hmm, what about the *readiness/liveness probe failures happening at 1-2s after pod start*? Those are startup. But 6l4dm's liveness failure at 08:29:20 is 12 min after start — steady state.

Wait, could this be a thundering herd on the probe: kubelet runs probes; the probe binary connects... 1s timeout. CPU throttling during the request burst → >1s to accept. Since the pod's CPU limit is 200m and request 100m, and Go service handles 175 req/45s... 200m is plenty normally.
